source: vois-tokens/references/*.md (18 files; excludes anti-slop.md and hooks.md — see note)
note: anti-slop.md (DS-SLOP-*) is intentionally excluded: it is self-declared judgment-only content graded by reading the code, not a lookup table (see references/anti-slop.md). hooks.md (DS-HOOKS) documents an automated-check tool, not a rule source. Both stay Markdown. The optional `engines` field on a rule (`["tailwind"]` or `["stylex"]`) marks it as specific to one styling engine; a rule with no `engines` field applies under either. Every rule also has `verification`: `detector` (a check in scripts/registry.mjs catches some or all violations of it, named in `detector`; passing the check does not prove the rule is met, and gaps are listed in references/hooks.md), `spec` (a chart-spec check), `rendered` (needs the page rendered) or `judgment` (an agent reads the code). It says how a rule can be checked, which is a different question from `enforcement` (whether a hook may deny the edit) and `severity` (how much the rule weighs).

rules.rule: Every interactive element has a hit area of at least var(--hit-area-min) in both dimensions. The visual element can be smaller. Extend the hit area with a pseudo-element, and never size the visible control with this token. On a coarse pointer (any-pointer: coarse) the minimum is var(--hit-area-coarse) (48).

`:focus-visible` — triggers only when the browser determines a visible focus indicator is needed. This covers keyboard navigation and assistive technology, but not mouse clicks. Use this for focus rings on buttons and links
Never remove `outline` without providing a `:focus-visible` replacement.
Minimum contrast ratio: 4.5:1 for normal text (under 18px regular, under 14px bold); 3:1 for large text (18px+ regular, 14px+ bold) and for UI components and graphical objects.
`<button>` for actions. `<a>` for navigation. Not `<div onClick>`.
Form inputs need associated `<label>` elements, not just placeholder text.
Icon-only buttons need `aria-label`.
Decorative icons need `aria-hidden="true"`.
Error messages need `aria-live="polite"` or `role="alert"`.
Images need `alt`. Decorative images get `alt=""`, not a missing alt attribute.
Use `<ul>` or `<ol>` for lists of items. Don't use a stack of `<div>` siblings when the content is semantically a list.

Use `
` only for intentional line breaks in content (addresses, poems). Never use it to create visual spacing between elements — that's a layout problem.
`loading="lazy"` on all images that aren't in the initial viewport. Skip it on hero images and above-the-fold content — those should load immediately.
rules.applies_when: images not in the initial viewport
rules.does_not_apply_when: hero images and above-the-fold content — those should load immediately

rules.rule: `<time datetime="...">` for dates and times. The `datetime` attribute is machine-readable; the element content is human-readable.
Don't use heading elements (`<h1>`–`<h6>`) just to get a certain font size. Use them for document structure. Style with CSS.
`<fieldset>` and `<legend>` for groups of related form controls (radio groups, checkbox groups). Don't skip this — screen readers announce the group label with each input.
Never use color as the only signal for state. Error, success, and warning states always need a secondary indicator — an icon, a text label, or both.

Focus indicators inherit component geometry. A focus indicator is an external ring: `outline: var(--focus-ring-width) solid var(--border-state-focus)` with `outline-offset: var(--focus-ring-offset)` (2px and 2px). Keep the control's own 1px border and its size: never swap the border for a thicker one, and never set `border-radius` on focus, because the browser draws an outline at the control's radius plus the offset. Where the ring would be clipped (an item in a scrolling or `overflow` container) draw it inside with a negative offset in the same color. Keep the ring when the field is in error. The ring color meets 3:1 on every surface in both themes.
Every dialog has an accessible name (DialogTitle or AlertDialogTitle, visually hidden if the design shows none). An AlertDialog also has a description that says what will happen.
First focus in a dialog: Cancel in a destructive AlertDialog (never the destructive button), the first field in a form dialog, the primary action in a confirmation that is not destructive.
When a dialog closes, focus returns to the element that opened it. If that element is gone, focus goes to the nearest sensible place, never to the top of the page.

Escape closes a dialog, and a click on the scrim closes a Dialog (not an AlertDialog: Radix blocks that on purpose). Block Escape and the scrim only while closing would lose money, a delete or a legal step in progress, and keep a visible Cancel when you do.
Anything the user can do by dragging can also be done with a single tap or the arrow keys (WCAG 2.2 criterion 2.5.7, Dragging Movements).
UI animations: under `300ms` as a default.
Large elements (drawers, bottom sheets, modals entering): up to `500ms`.
Never animate keyboard-triggered interactions. Repeated actions feel slower when animated. Keyboard users feel this.
rules.applies_when: keyboard-triggered interactions specifically

rules.rule: Always respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Users who set this have real reasons — vestibular disorders, epilepsy, motion sensitivity.
Never animate from `scale(0)`. Start at `0.9` or higher. Zero-scale animations feel mechanical. The one exception is an icon swap, which follows `DS-SURFACE-014`.
Set `transform-origin` to the trigger point. A dropdown expands from the button that opened it. A tooltip appears from the element it describes. The default `center` is wrong in most cases.
Tailwind v4's `hover:` only fires on devices that support hover. If writing raw CSS, guard hover styles with `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`.

Use `scale(0.96)` on button press. Never go below `0.95` — anything smaller reads as exaggerated rather than tactile. Not every button needs this — add a `static` prop to disable it where the motion would be distracting (e.g. inside a list with frequent clicks).

Set `will-change` on GPU-compositable properties (`transform`, `opacity`, `filter`, `clip-path`) to pre-promote an element to its own GPU layer and avoid a one-frame stutter on first animation. It does nothing for `width`, `height`, `top`, `left`, `background`, `border`, or `color`. Add it only when you actually notice first-frame stutter, not preemptively — each layer costs memory.
rules.applies_when: only after first-frame stutter is actually observed on a GPU-compositable property — not preemptively

rules.rule: Timing and easing come from motion tokens (`var(--motion-duration-*)`, `var(--motion-ease-*)`, or `motion-tokens.ts` for Motion). Component code holds no literal durations, `cubic-bezier(...)` curves, or numeric easing arrays. Only the token file (`motion-tokens.{css,scss,ts,js}`) may define them.
rules.applies_when: any transition, animation, or Motion component in code or CSS

rules.rule: The slow duration token is for large elements only (drawers, sheets, modals entering). It can run up to 500ms. Any other UI animation stays under 300ms, whichever token it uses.
rules.applies_when: a slow duration token is applied to an element that is not a large surface

rules.rule: A morph runs inside one duration token. Old content leaves while new content arrives, so the whole morph takes one token, never two added together. Out-then-in in sequence doubles the time and breaks `DS-ANIMATION-001`.
rules.applies_when: a label, text or icon morph that animates the old value out and the new value in

rules.rule: A tray (a persistent bottom container that shows one step at a time) is one element. Steps swap inside it and its height follows the new step. It never unmounts between steps.
rules.applies_when: a multi-step bottom sheet or drawer where each step has its own content

rules.rule: When a shared element travels between views, the content it leaves behind may dim and blur. The blur never exceeds the value in `DS-SURFACE-014`, and the travelling element is never blurred.
rules.applies_when: a shared element transfer between two full views or from a list item into its detail

rules.rule: Springs are allowed when `bounce` is `0` and the duration comes from a motion token (`motionSpring` in `motion-tokens.ts`). A transition that is retargeted mid-flight continues from its current position and velocity, not from the start.
rules.applies_when: a spring transition, or an animation the user can interrupt

rules.rule: Delight never gates the task and never carries meaning alone. A loop pauses under `prefers-reduced-motion` and while the page is hidden, nothing flashes more than three times a second, and a one-off occasion effect plays once and can be skipped.
rules.applies_when: a decorative or expressive animation, an ambient loop, or an easter egg

rules.rule: Never hardcode hex values. Use CSS tokens.
Never use Tailwind's built-in color palette (`blue-500`, `red-400`, etc.) if a token exists for it. The token is always preferred.
Color cannot be the only signal. Error states, success states, warnings — always pair color with an icon, label, or text. Never rely on color alone.
60/30/10 distribution: roughly 60% neutral, 30% complementary/secondary, 10% accent/brand. This prevents visual stress and keeps hierarchy clear.
Decorative icons that add no information get `aria-hidden="true"`. Don't let screen readers announce them.
Dark mode is implemented via `@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *))`. Every color token must have a dark mode value.
Before shipping any component, verify both light and dark mode manually.

Status color comes from four semantic roles: `info`, `positive`, `negative`, `notice`. Each role has a token in the Base layer and in every System layer, named after the Figma variables: `--base-{role}`, `--bg-{role}`, `--text-{role}`, `--border-{role}`, `--icon-{role}`. Components that show status (Alert, Badge, Toast, inline validation, banners) use these tokens. Never a palette class or a literal color for status, and never a one-off token invented for it.

Pick the status role by meaning, not by hue. `info` is neutral context. `positive` is success or completion. `negative` is an error, a failure, or a destructive action. `notice` is caution or something that needs attention before it becomes an error. There is no separate `destructive` token: a destructive Button reads `--base-negative`, and `destructive` is only the shadcn variant name. Older names (`--color-destructive`, `--color-success`, `--color-warning`, `--color-{role}-surface`) become the Figma tokens: `warning` is `notice`, a surface is `--bg-{role}`.
Check the manifest first. If `<Button>`, `<AlertBanner>`, or `<DataTable>` exists, use it. Don't rebuild it.

Use a typed, centralized variant-authorship mechanism for all variant styling — Class Variance Authority (cva) under Tailwind, composed `stylex.create()` keys under StyleX (see `[DS-STYLEX-004]`). No ad-hoc className/style ternaries.
Use `data-slot` attributes for styling component internals — don't reach into component children with arbitrary CSS selectors.
New-York style is the default for shadcn. The "default" style is deprecated.
Components use a 2-layer architecture: Radix UI (or another unstyled primitive library) for structure/behavior, the project's styling engine — Tailwind or StyleX — for style. Don't collapse these.
When using a component with variants, use the most semantically appropriate variant. Don't default to `default` when `destructive`, `ghost`, or `outline` is more correct.

Control heights come from the size tokens. Button heights are 28 (`--size-action-medium`), 36 (`--size-action-large`) and 48 (`--size-action-x-large`), and 36 is the default on web, 48 on native. The circular action is 56 (`--size-action-circular`) and no other action or control is 56 (an avatar can be, and so can the `icon-lg` icon button on a coarse pointer, DS-ICON-003). Input and Select are `--size-field-web` (36) on web and `--size-field-native` (48) on native. `--size-field-compact` (32) is only for an inline field nested in a table or a dense row. A Button next to a field matches the field's height.
Trap focus using `inert`. When a modal opens, add `inert` to all content outside the modal. This blocks keyboard and screen reader access to background content without manual focus trapping
rules.applies_when: custom (non-Radix) dialog/modal implementations — Radix UI handles inert/focus-trap automatically

rules.rule: Prevent scroll bleed. Add `overscroll-behavior: contain` to the modal's scrollable container so scrolling inside doesn't scroll the page behind it
rules.applies_when: custom (non-Radix) dialog/modal implementations — Radix UI handles this automatically

rules.rule: Prevent layout shift. When a modal opens and the page scrollbar disappears, the layout jumps. Fix it with `scrollbar-gutter` on `html`
rules.applies_when: custom (non-Radix) dialog/modal implementations — Radix UI handles this automatically

rules.rule: The body of a dialog scrolls. The header and the footer stay in view. A tall dialog never scrolls its title or actions away.

A dialog footer has a primary action and a secondary action (Cancel), both right-aligned. Typically that is all. A third action is a ghost or link button on the left, and only when the dialog is wider than 400px.

Never nest modals. A second step replaces the content of the same dialog (push a view with a Back control) or becomes a page. A destructive confirmation from inside a dialog or sheet replaces its content the same way.
Never use a modal for navigation. A list of places to go is a menu or a page.
No inline styles for values that have token equivalents.
Never use `#id` selectors for styling. IDs have high specificity and make overrides painful.
Keep selectors shallow. If your selector has more than 2 levels of nesting, you're coupling styles to DOM structure. Add a class instead.
Use `:is()` to group selectors without multiplying specificity.
Use `:where()` when you want zero-specificity base styles that are easy to override.
Separate layout from visual concerns.
Use `em` for breakpoints, not `px`. Breakpoints in `em` respect the user's browser font size preference and scale correctly when users zoom.
The backdrop behind a modal is a separate concern from the modal's own shadow. Use the scrim token `--bg-overlay-dark`, not a darker shadow and not a literal color.

Use the five elevation tiers from Figma, `--shadow-base` to `--shadow-xlarge`, and match each element to the tier in `data/elevation-map.json`. Card, Choice Card and the segmented indicator rest at Base. Card hover, resting Choice Card hover, Switch knob and Hover Card are Small. Menus and select lists are Medium and pair with the dropdown z-index. Dialog and Tooltip are Large and pair with the overlay or modal z-index. XLarge is only for a dragged item or a full-screen surface. Layers run in role order (page, dropdown, overlay, modal), so don't put a heavier shadow on a lower layer than on the one above it. The exception is a popup opened from a dialog (menu, select, hover card, tooltip): it stacks above the modal and keeps its own lighter tier.

Move an element by at most one tier when its state changes, using the map in `data/elevation-map.json`: hover goes up one tier at most and never down, pressed goes down one tier or to flat, a dragged item goes to a high tier, a disabled element is flat or unchanged. Focus never changes elevation. The focus ring is the focus indicator (`DS-A11Y-018`).
A resting card keeps a Base or Small shadow. A static section that only groups content stays flat (`DS-SLOP-010`). Do not give a plain section a shadow just to look like a card.

In dark mode, never use a shadow alone. Base and Small carry no shadow: a lighter fill step than the parent and a 1px hairline border carry them. Medium and up use a blacker shadow plus the hairline. A 4 to 5% black shadow is invisible on a dark surface. The tokens exist: `--elevation-surface-small`, `--elevation-surface-raised` and `--elevation-surface-popup` (a menu, select list or hover card, one step above a Dialog) for the fills, `--elevation-hairline` for an edge (transparent in light), and `.dark` redefines `--shadow-base` to `--shadow-xlarge`, so a component that reads a tier token gets the dark shadow for free. Set the fill and the edge yourself from the surface and hairline tokens. Do not hand-write dark values.

A panel docked to an edge casts its shadow away from that edge, not on all sides. Right-docked: negative x. Left-docked: positive x. Bottom-docked: negative y. Top-docked: positive y. Centered: x is 0. Use a negative spread so the shadow does not leak past the panel. Use the directional token for the side: `--shadow-large-right`, `-left`, `-bottom` or `-top` (Large only today), and record the side in the map's `dock` field.

Do not write a raw shadow with blur: a `box-shadow` or `boxShadow` literal, a `shadow-[...]` value, or a Tailwind default such as `shadow-md`. Use a tier token (`--shadow-base` to `--shadow-xlarge`, or a glass surface's `--glass-shadow-*`, DS-GLASS-009). A zero-blur ring (spread only, such as an edge or a checkbox ring) is not a tier and is allowed.
Show at most two distinct shadow tiers at rest in one view. If a third seems needed, the layout needs fewer levels, not more shadow.
Use Large and XLarge only for overlays, hover and a dragged item. Never on a static element in the page.
Use an inset shadow only for a recessed or pressed element. A zero-blur inset ring used as a border or a focus or checked ring is not an elevation shadow and is allowed.
To animate between Medium or heavier tiers, cross-fade the opacity of a pre-drawn layer. Do not animate `box-shadow` on large shadows. Animating a 1 to 2px ring is fine.
Check text and border contrast on every elevated fill, not only on the page color. A lighter dark-mode fill step must still keep text at 4.5:1 and a control edge at 3:1.

Frosted glass is opt-in and goes only on chrome and floating layers: a sticky nav bar, tab bar or toolbar; a menu, popover or dropdown; a dialog, sheet or command palette; an icon button floating over an image, video or map (Button variant="glass"). Never on the content layer (body text, a data table, a form, a card in a list). At most 3 glass surfaces in one viewport.

Glass has three tiers and no more. Subtle (chips, badges, hover): blur --glass-blur-subtle (8), saturate 150%. Standard (sticky nav or toolbar, menus): --glass-blur-standard (16), 160%. Strong (dialog, sheet, command palette, always over the scrim): --glass-blur-strong (24), 180%. Fill, edge, highlight and shadow come from --glass-tint-*, --glass-stroke-*, --glass-highlight-* and --glass-shadow-* of the same tier. Dark tint is white at low alpha, never black. Corners come from the shape roles, not the tier.

Every backdrop-filter has a -webkit-backdrop-filter with the same value (WebkitBackdropFilter in a style object). Safari before 18 reads only the prefixed one. Tailwind's backdrop-blur utilities write both.
The backdrop blur radius is var(--glass-blur-subtle), -standard or -strong. Never a literal (blur(12px), backdrop-blur-md, backdrop-blur-[20px]), and never more than 24 on a panel.

Never animate backdrop-filter: no transition, @keyframes or motion prop (animate, initial, exit, while*) that changes it. The browser re-blurs every frame. Fade the surface's opacity instead, or show it at once.

Never put a glass element inside another one, or inside a backdrop root (an ancestor with opacity under 1, a filter, mask, clip-path, mix-blend-mode or its own backdrop-filter). The inner blur then reaches only up to that ancestor, not the page.

Fallback first: the base style is the opaque elevation fill of the layer (--elevation-surface-small, -popup or -raised). An @supports test for backdrop-filter or its -webkit- twin lowers the fill to the tint and adds the blur. Under prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce, the opaque fill comes back and backdrop-filter is none.

Check text on glass against the lightest and the darkest patch that can sit behind it, in both themes and at more than one scroll position: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text and controls. If it fails, use a stronger tier or a 35% black dimming layer over bright media. Never lower the bar. No accent-colored text or links on glass.

A glass surface's float shadow is its tier's --glass-shadow-* token, and its top highlight is a zero-blur inset 0 1px 0 var(--glass-highlight-*). The glass shadow tokens count as tier tokens under DS-ELEVATION-007. The strong tier sits over the one modal scrim, --bg-overlay-dark; there is no second scrim for glass.

In Figma, fill a glass layer with Component/Glass/Tint-* (under 100% alpha, or the background blur does not show), stroke it 1px inside with Stroke-*, and apply the Glass/<Tier> effect style (Glass/Dark/<Tier> in a Dark frame). Do not combine Figma's Glass effect with Background blur on one layer. Use the same blur numbers in both and compare a browser screenshot with the canvas before changing either.

Use a single stroke width across the icon set — 1.5px for the default (lucide-react/Radix Icons default). Don't mix stroke weights within the same screen; it reads as a design system bug, not a deliberate choice.

If an icon's surrounding text size doesn't map cleanly to one of the four defined sizes (16/20/24/32px), round to the nearest one rather than introducing an arbitrary size. The Button sets one more on its own, a 28px glyph for `icon-lg` on a coarse pointer (DS-ICON-003); never set 28 by hand.

Icon-button sizes follow the Button heights: `icon-sm` 28 with a 16 glyph, `icon` 36 with a 20 glyph (the default), `icon-lg` 48 with a 24 glyph. On a coarse pointer (`@media (any-pointer: coarse)`, not the screen width) they step up to 36/20, 48/24 and 56/28. The target is at least 44 (48 on a coarse pointer) through invisible expansion (DS-A11Y-001). Never smaller than `icon-sm`, except a button inside a field and a chip's remove control (DS-ICON-006). One icon-button size and one glyph size per row.

Targets of neighboring icon buttons can touch but never overlap. The gap between two visuals is at least the larger of 8px and the target minus the visual: 16 between `icon-sm` buttons and 8 between `icon` or `icon-lg` buttons on a fine pointer, 12 between `icon-sm` buttons on a coarse pointer. If a row cannot fit the gap, move actions into a menu.

An icon-only button has an accessible name that says what it does (`aria-label="Add to favorites"`, not "Heart"), from `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` or `sr-only` text. A Tooltip with the same text shows on hover and focus and never replaces the name. Use icon-only buttons only for actions everyone knows (search, close, add, delete, more, favorite, play).

Place icon buttons by role: app bar `icon` with at most 4 actions plus a "More actions" menu; dense desktop toolbar `icon-sm`; table row `icon-sm` with at most 3 visible; close a dialog, sheet or panel with `icon` in the top end corner, `aria-label="Close"`; a button inside a field is an InputGroupButton `icon-sm` (28) or `icon-xs` (24), never taller than the field, with a 44 target (48 on a coarse pointer); bottom nav on touch `icon-lg` with a label, navigation only; a primary on-screen action `icon-lg`, with emphasis from the variant. Actions under an AI chat message are `icon-sm` with no background, at most 4 in the row; there is no 20px or 24px icon button. A chip's remove control may be smaller only inside a chip under 28px tall, when its target reaches 24px with spacing (WCAG 2.5.8), and never as the only way to do a destructive action.

Icon buttons come in styles by background: no background (`variant="ghost"`, the default, for toolbars, app bars, table rows and actions under a chat message) Soft (`variant="soft"`, a light gray resting fill `--action-icon-soft-resting`, for a button that must read as a button at rest on a plain surface) and Glass (`variant="glass"`, the glass subtle tier, only over an image, video or map, DS-GLASS-001). Soft's hover and pressed fills are one step above the ghost's. One style per row. Sizes, gaps and tap areas are the same for every style.
Stop using `vh`. It breaks on mobile because browser chrome changes the available height as you scroll. Use the right unit for the context
For pages with significant vertical scroll, use `content-visibility: auto` on sections that are far below the fold to skip rendering them until they approach the viewport
Mobile-first. No prefix = mobile baseline. `md:`, `lg:` are progressive enhancements.

Test at the start of each grid class, narrow (360px), sm (600px), md (768px) and lg (1024px), before considering a component done. These are the values of --width-viewport-min and the breakpoint tokens in DS-GRID-001.
Use container queries for component-level responsiveness. Use breakpoints for layout-level responsiveness.
Touch targets, font sizes, and contrast ratios must meet minimums at every breakpoint.
Don't build desktop-first and assume it'll work on mobile. It won't.

Preserve task hierarchy before shrinking type. Identify the primary task/content on the screen and keep it at a comfortable, legible size at every breakpoint; let secondary and tertiary content absorb the constraint first.

When content doesn't fit, prefer reflow, then collapse, then hide, in that order, before shrinking text or spacing to cram the same layout into less room. Shrinking is the last resort and never overrides the DS-RESPONSIVE-004 minimums.

Below --breakpoint-md a dialog that holds a choice (confirm, select, stepper, slider) is a bottom sheet: at most 90dvh tall, a stacked footer with the primary button on top, a visible Close or Cancel button, and dvh for its height.
Below --breakpoint-md a dialog that takes text is a full-screen form, not a bottom sheet: a 56 tall header, and a footer at the bottom of the scroll area so the keyboard cannot cover it.
A bottom sheet and a full-screen form pad their edges with env(safe-area-inset-bottom), env(safe-area-inset-left) and env(safe-area-inset-right).
No `padding-bottom`/`margin-top` used to space siblings — use `gap` on the parent.
No wrapper divs that serve no layout purpose.
`min-width: 0` on flex children containing text or overflow-prone content.
Images with set dimensions need `object-fit`.
Use `aspect-ratio` instead of the padding-top percentage hack.
All spacing must be divisible by 4 or 8. The only exception is --grid-margin and --grid-gutter between their end values (DS-GRID-004).
Use `gap` for layout spacing between elements. Use padding for internal component spacing. Avoid margin for layout — it's harder to reason about and doesn't compose well with flex/grid.
Tailwind v4 note: Dynamic spacing utilities accept any value without arbitrary syntax. This makes it easy to accidentally use off-grid values. Don't. Stay on the scale.
Verify spacing holds at every responsive breakpoint before considering a component done.
Mismatched radii on nested elements is one of the most common things that makes UI feel off.

If padding between the two surfaces is larger than `24px`, treat them as independent surfaces and pick each radius on its own — forcing strict concentric math at that distance looks over-engineered, not intentional.
rules.applies_when: padding between the two nested surfaces exceeds 24px

rules.rule: When geometric centering looks wrong, align optically instead.
Buttons with text + icon: use slightly less padding on the icon side. Rule of thumb: `icon-side padding = text-side padding - 2px`.
Play button triangles: the geometric center of a triangle is not its visual center. Shift right ~2px.

Asymmetric icons (stars, arrows, carets): fix the SVG's `viewBox`/path directly if possible, so no compensating margin is needed in component code. Fall back to a small margin only if you can't touch the SVG.

For cards, containers, and bordered buttons that exist to show depth or elevation, prefer a layered `box-shadow` over a solid `border`. Shadows use transparency so they adapt to any background color or image; solid border colors only look right on the background they were tuned for.
Do not apply this to dividers (`border-b`, `border-t`, list separators) or anything whose job is layout separation, not depth. Those stay as borders.
Add a subtle `1px` outline to images for consistent depth, especially in systems that already use borders/shadows elsewhere.

Never use a near-black/near-white from the palette (slate-900, zinc-900, `#0a0a0a`, etc.) and never match it to the accent/ink color. A tinted outline picks up the surface color underneath and reads as dirt on the image edge.

Don't animate one large container on enter. Split into semantic chunks (title, description, actions) and stagger with ~100ms delay between groups. For titles, splitting into individual words with ~80ms stagger reads even better, but isn't required for routine UI.

Use `initial={false}` on `AnimatePresence` to skip enter animations on first page load for elements already in their default state (icon swaps, tabs, toggles). Don't apply it to staged page-hero entrances that depend on the `initial` prop to fire at all — verify on a hard refresh.
Exits should be softer than enters — the user's attention is already moving to the next thing.
When an icon swaps state (play→pause, like→liked, hover-revealed actions), animate `opacity` + `scale` + `blur` instead of toggling visibility. Use exactly these values — don't deviate

StyleX requires the official Babel plugin (or the equivalent bundler/SWC plugin) wired into the build before any `stylex.create()` call does anything — styles are inert without it. Confirm the plugin is configured before writing StyleX styles in a project.

Define tokens with `stylex.defineVars()` and reference them from `stylex.create()`. Never use a literal value in `stylex.create()` where a defined token exists — the StyleX-side version of `[DS-CSS-001]`/`[DS-COLOR-001]`.
Use `stylex.createTheme()` to override a `defineVars()` group for theme variants (dark mode, brand variants). Don't hand-roll a second, parallel token set.

Compose variant styling from multiple `stylex.create()` keys merged in `stylex.props()`, most-specific override passed last. This is StyleX's equivalent of `[DS-COMPONENT-002]`'s variant-authorship requirement — no ad-hoc conditional style objects.

Don't use an inline `style={{}}` prop where a `stylex.create()` key already covers the value. Inline styles have higher specificity than any StyleX-generated class and silently win over intended variant styling.

Use `stylex.defineConsts()` for breakpoints and other compile-time constants instead of repeating literal media-query strings. Author breakpoint values in `em`, not `px` — same rule as `[DS-CSS-007]`.

Replace `@layer base` with `@theme` for the names Tailwind generates utilities from. The Vois tokens themselves live in `:root` and `.dark` (DS-TOKEN-003), and `@theme inline` aliases expose the ones a utility or component library needs.
Use `@import "tailwindcss"` instead of `@tailwind base / components / utilities`.
Arbitrary values (`w-[237px]`, `mt-[13px]`) are a smell. If you need an arbitrary value, either it belongs on the spacing scale or it's a missing token. Round it or flag it.
No `!important` except for utility overrides you explicitly own and document.
Never `transition: all`. List properties explicitly: `transition: background-color 150ms ease-out, transform 150ms ease-out`.
Use no more than 3 text styles in any single component or section.
Never skip heading levels. `h1` then `h2` then `h3`. Never `h1` directly to `h3`.
Use the monospace variant for all numeric data — prices, counts, measurements, timestamps. Add `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` when numbers appear in columns or need to align.
Font size communicates hierarchy. If two things feel equally important, one of them should be deprioritized.
Always reference the token (`font-[var(--font-heading)]`) rather than a font name directly. If the workspace swaps the font, components update automatically without code changes.
Apply `text-wrap: balance` to all headings (H0 through H3) by default.
Apply `text-wrap: pretty` to body copy in articles, descriptions, and anywhere text wraps across multiple lines.
Cap text containers at `65ch`. The `ch` unit is relative to the current font's character width, so this stays readable at any font size.
Use `…` (the ellipsis character), not `...` (three periods)
Use curly quotes `"` `"` not straight `"`
Loading states end with ellipsis character: `"Loading…"` not `"Loading..."`
Active voice: "Save changes" not "Changes will be saved"
Specific button labels: "Delete project" not "Confirm" or "OK"
Error messages tell the user what to do next, not just what went wrong
Form containers use max-width: var(--width-form-max). No hardcoded width values.
Single-line fields use max-width: var(--width-field-max) by default. Short fixed-format values use var(--width-field-narrow). Only textareas may extend to var(--width-form-max).
Layouts must hold at var(--width-viewport-min) with no horizontal scroll.
Desktop dialogs use max-width: var(--width-dialog-sm) or var(--width-dialog-lg). No hardcoded dialog widths. Which tier applies is decided in vois-patterns PATH-D-SIZE.
Text areas that grow with their content use field-sizing: content (Tailwind v4: field-sizing-content). No JavaScript autosizing: no scrollHeight measuring, ResizeObserver, or autosize libraries.
Always set an explicit inline-size with field-sizing: content. Content sizing also shrinks the width, and an unset width collapses to a sliver.

Set min-block-size and max-block-size from the line-count tokens using the lh unit plus the field's block padding. Do not rely on the rows attribute for the minimum, because browsers ignore rows under field-sizing: content. Scroll inside the field with overflow-y: auto at the maximum.
Wrap field-sizing styles in @supports (field-sizing: content). Keep the rows attribute and resize: vertical as the fallback for browsers without support.

Pick the grid class from the region width, not the window width. Four classes: narrow (4 columns), sm (8), md (8) and lg (12), starting at --width-viewport-min, --breakpoint-sm, --breakpoint-md and --breakpoint-lg.

Window width picks the navigation: bottom bar below --breakpoint-md, a --nav-rail rail from there, a --nav-sidebar sidebar from --breakpoint-lg. The site shell has a top bar and no side navigation. Region width is window width minus navigation width.
Content stops at --grid-content-max and centers. A page whose template says frame fill (dashboard, data grid, report, split view) opts out and fills the region.

Margin and gutter come from --grid-margin and --grid-gutter, never a raw value. Each is a line between two anchor points on region width, held flat outside them. The token source stores four plain numbers per line (min, max, min-at, max-at) and the two names above are generated from them: clamp() on the web, the same line in code on native. The end values sit on the spacing scale, the values between them do not, so DS-SPACING-001 does not apply to these two tokens.
The real margin is the larger of --grid-margin and the safe-area inset on that side. Use start and end sides, never left and right.

A component measures the space it is given, not the screen: a container query on the web, LayoutBuilder, BoxWithConstraints or GeometryReader on native. Never branch on device type, device model or orientation.

A collection holds max(1, min(cap[windowClass], floor((inner + gutter) / (itemMin + gutter)))) columns. cap comes from the page template, inner is the region width minus both margins held at --grid-content-max (no hold on a fill page; a container narrower than the region uses its own width), gutter is --grid-gutter at the region width, and itemMin is the item token the template names.
Larger text raises itemMin, so the column count drops. It never changes the grid, margins or gutters.
A region is a track: fluid, a fraction such as 2fr, auto, or a token name. A split must fit the columns of the current class: an 8 column class splits 4 and 4 or 5 and 3, never 6 and 6.
One token unit is one CSS pixel, one dp on Android and one point on iOS. Tokens are plain numbers that every platform reads the same way.
Use a push panel (inline, moves the main content) when people need to see the page and the panel together. Use an overlay panel (floats over the page) for a task that ends.
Below --breakpoint-md every panel is full screen. No push, no half-width overlay.
From --breakpoint-md a panel pushes only if window width minus --nav-rail minus the panel width leaves at least --main-min. Otherwise it is an overlay.

While a push panel is open, the app shell keeps the full sidebar only if window width minus --nav-sidebar minus the panel width leaves at least --main-min. Otherwise the sidebar shows as the rail until the panel closes. Do this before turning the panel into an overlay.
A push panel is --panel-push-default wide. If people can resize it, keep it between --panel-push-min and --panel-push-max. The main content never goes below --main-min.

An overlay uses a size tier (--panel-overlay-sm, --panel-overlay-md or --panel-overlay-lg). Its width is the smallest of the tier and half the window width rounded down to a multiple of 4, and never under --panel-overlay-min.

A list with a detail pane shows both side by side only if each pane gets at least --pane-min. Otherwise it behaves like a phone: the list alone, and the detail opens as its own screen with a back control.
Panel and pane widths are token names. Never a raw number in code, in a template or in a design spec.

A table has exactly one scroll owner, chosen on purpose. A sticky header sticks to its nearest scroll-container ancestor, and any overflow other than visible or clip creates one, so nothing between the header and the intended owner may change that by accident.

A complex table's wrapper owns both axes: overflow: auto with a bounded block size, a sticky header inside it, scrollbar-gutter: stable, overscroll-behavior-x: contain, and scroll-padding-block-start equal to the header height.
A simple table sets no overflow on its wrapper, so its sticky header sticks to the page (offset by any fixed app header), and it never scrolls sideways.
Do not use overflow: auto clip, or overflow-x: auto with overflow-y: clip, to keep a header sticky to the page. clip computes to hidden next to auto, which is still a scroll container.
Every flex or grid ancestor between the app shell and a table wrapper has min-inline-size: 0 and min-block-size: 0, so the table neither widens the page nor loses its bounded height.

A pinned first column uses position: sticky with inset-inline-start: 0 and an opaque background. Layers are small local z-index values (pinned column 1, header row 2, corner cell 3) inside a stacking context made by isolation: isolate on the scroll owner, so they never outrank an overlay. Add scroll-padding-inline-start equal to the column width.
Tables with sticky cells use border-collapse: separate with border-spacing: 0. Collapsed borders do not travel with sticky cells.
Table layout changes key off the container, not the viewport: container-type: inline-size on an element outside the scroll wrapper, and @container (width < 37.5em) for the narrow layout.
Use table-layout: fixed with explicit column widths, text-overflow: ellipsis on text cells, right-aligned numbers with tabular-nums, and left-aligned text.

Style table scrollbars with scrollbar-width: thin and scrollbar-color from an existing neutral token such as the muted foreground. No ::-webkit-scrollbar. Do not hide the scrollbar on a table that scrolls sideways.
scrollbar-gutter: stable on the scroll owner, so header and body columns stay aligned when a scrollbar appears.
overscroll-behavior-x: contain on the scroll owner. Do not contain the vertical axis.
scroll-padding-block-start equal to the sticky header height on the scroll owner, so focused rows are not hidden under it.

A complex table that scrolls on both axes scrolls one axis per gesture: a wheel handler (passive: false, ctrlKey passes through) that scrolls only the dominant axis, shared as one hook, with an opt-out. Simple tables do not use it. Leave touch alone.

A scroll owner has tabindex="0", role="region", and an aria-label. Keep real table elements, a button inside a sortable th, and aria-sort on the sorted th. Use role="grid" only with arrow-key cell navigation.
Paginate by default. Virtualize only for database-style grids with thousands of rows, and test the sticky header and pinned column with a long scroll.
Highlights for just-added or just-saved rows and any scroll-shadow transition respect prefers-reduced-motion.
A table that scrolls sideways shows a cue that more content exists, such as an edge shadow on the pinned column or a partly visible column, because overlay scrollbars are hidden until scroll.

Header height and row height per density come from the table_sizes tokens. Check the workspace token set first. If one is missing, propose adding it, never hardcode. The space above a complex table and a fixed app header's height are set by the page, not tokens, and the component supplies a fallback.
Apply the marketing type and spacing rules only on marketing surfaces (landing pages, product marketing, public site pages). Product UI keeps DS-TYPOGRAPHY and DS-SPACING as written.
The display face (`--font-heading`) carries display and h2 only and is never used below 28px. The text face (`--font-body`) carries everything else. Both roles can be one family at different weights.
One display headline per page and one h2 per section.

Use the marketing type scale as a starting point: display 40/44 mobile and 72/76 desktop, h2 28/34 and 44/50, h3 20/26 and 24/30, lead 18/26 and 20/30, body 16/24 and 17/26, small 14/20 and 15/22. Values are estimates. Keep the ratios and adjust per site.
Cap marketing body text at `56ch`. This replaces the 65ch cap in DS-TYPOGRAPHY-008 on marketing surfaces. Headings may run narrower.

The gap between sections is about 4x the gap between a section heading and its content, and 12 to 15x the gap between a heading and its body text. If a page feels cramped, widen the section gap first, then cut content. Do not add dividers to compensate.
Keep the gap inside a block smaller than the gap between blocks. If they match, the page reads as one pile.

On marketing surfaces, section-to-section gaps may exceed 128px, up to 240px, in steps of 8, using a spacing token. This is an exception to the allowed-values list in spacing.md. DS-SPACING-001 (divisible by 4 or 8) still holds.

Tokens come in four layers: Global palettes, Base, System and Component. Use the most specific layer that fits: a component's own Component tokens, then System tokens. Component code never names a Global palette step directly.
A token's CSS name is its Web code syntax in Figma. Don't invent a name or derive one by hand from the Figma path. If a variable has no code syntax, flag it.

Define the tokens in `:root` (light) and `.dark` (dark), not in `@theme`: Tailwind v4 reads `--text-*` in `@theme` as font sizes. Expose the names Tailwind or a component library needs through `@theme inline` aliases.

The Base layer sets the brand (`--base-brand` primary, `--base-accent-solid` and `--base-accent-soft` accent). Because the primary action states and the accent System tokens point at palette steps directly in the current Figma file, thirteen color tokens carry the brand: `--base-brand`, `--base-accent-solid`, `--base-accent-soft`, `--action-primary-resting`, `--action-primary-hover`, `--action-primary-focus`, `--action-primary-pressed`, `--action-primary-disabled`, `--action-primary-text`, `--bg-accent`, `--text-accent`, `--icon-accent`, `--border-accent`. So do the four font families (`--font-family-brand`, `--font-family-system`, `--font-family-written`, `--font-family-mono`). A brand theme overrides these seventeen and nothing else. A product's own brand stays in that product, not in this skill.

With shadcn/ui, point each shadcn variable at its Vois token: `background` at `--bg-background`; `foreground`, `card-foreground`, `popover-foreground`, `secondary-foreground` and `accent-foreground` at `--text-primary`; `card` at `--bg-card`; `popover` at `--elevation-surface-popup`, so a stock shadcn popover, menu or select list is one step above a Dialog in dark and matches the Vois menus; `primary` at `--action-primary-resting`; `primary-foreground` at `--action-primary-text`; `secondary` at `--action-secondary-resting`; `muted` at `--bg-subtle`; `muted-foreground` at `--text-secondary`; `accent` at `--bg-hover`; `destructive` at `--base-negative`; `border` at `--border-pretty`; `input` at `--input-border`; `ring` at `--border-state-focus`; `radius` at `--radii-8`, so shadcn's derived steps land on the Vois radius roles (`md` 6, `lg` 8, `xl` 12).

Choose a shape role (`--shape-sharp`, `--shape-subtle`, `--shape-rounded`, `--shape-soft`, `--shape-pill`, `--shape-circle`, `--shape-responsive-soft`, `--shape-responsive-elliptical`) before choosing a number, from the component's size, aspect ratio, prominence and content. Prefer, in order: the project's existing component, an existing shape role, a contextual adjustment within it, and a new value only when nothing fits.
rules.applies_when: any corner radius on a component, surface or media element

rules.rule: Controls (buttons, inputs, selects) keep the library's fixed control radius (`--shape-subtle`). Tags, chips, pill tabs, segmented controls and status indicators use `--shape-pill`; avatars and round icon buttons use `--shape-circle`. Don't turn a button or input into a pill unless the project's component already is one.
rules.applies_when: choosing the radius of a control, tag, chip, avatar or status indicator

rules.rule: Large visual surfaces whose size changes with the layout (hero media, large image-led cards, editorial and promo tiles) use `--shape-responsive-soft`: round corners that grow with the nearest container's width, clamped. The surface's wrapper declares `container-type: inline-size`. Structural UI (dialogs, menus, standard cards) keeps a fixed role even when large.
rules.applies_when: a hero, media, image-led or editorial surface that resizes with the layout

rules.rule: Use `--shape-responsive-elliptical` (a percentage per axis) only where an elliptical corner is intended, on a distinctive media surface. It is round only on a 3:2 box. For round corners that scale, use `--shape-responsive-soft`.
rules.applies_when: considering a percentage or elliptical border radius

rules.rule: Never write a one-off radius because it looks right (`rounded-[19px]`, `border-radius: 19px`). Use a shape role, or a `--radius-*` or `--radii-*` token within one. If no role fits, name the missing role and why instead of adding a number.
rules.applies_when: writing any border-radius value

rules.rule: The concentric rule (outer radius = inner radius + padding) applies between fixed roles only. Inside a proportional, elliptical or capsule parent, choose the child's role on its own.
rules.applies_when: a rounded element nested in a proportional, elliptical or capsule surface

rules.rule: Add continuous (squircle) corners as an enhancement on the soft and responsive roles only, behind a support check (`supports-[corner-shape:squircle]:[corner-shape:squircle]` or `@supports (corner-shape: squircle)`). `squircle` is `superellipse(2)`. A surface may tune it with `superellipse(n)` where `n` is from 1 to 4. Never `n` below 1 or `infinity`. Never on controls, pills or circles.
rules.applies_when: a soft or responsive-shape surface where smoother corners are wanted

rules.rule: Mark every question "Required" or "Optional" in words, not with an asterisk alone. Set `aria-required` on required questions. After a failed check set `aria-invalid`, put a specific error under the question, and move focus to the first error.
In a one-question-per-screen flow, moving to another question moves focus to the new question title and announces it. This holds for Next and for Back.
In a questionnaire, honour `prefers-reduced-motion` and also offer a visible Reduce motion control. Between questions use no slide or scale. An instant swap or a fade of 150ms or less is fine.

A poll or quiz result never relies on colour alone. The correct option carries a check icon and the words 'Correct answer'. The respondent's own pick carries the words 'Your answer'. Each row reads as text: label, percent, and count when shown. Bars are decorative (aria-hidden) and the bar fill has 3:1 contrast against its track.

When results appear, announce one short summary in a polite live region and move focus to the results heading. Do not announce every bar or every live update. Bars may animate for 400ms or less, and not at all with reduced motion (DS-A11Y-026).

In a questionnaire put the primary action in a sticky bar inside the scrolling container, not `position: fixed`, because the on-screen keyboard covers a fixed bar. Add `padding-bottom: calc(12px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`. Put errors above the input, between the label and the field.

Below 360px a 5-point Likert goes vertical if a point would be under 44px, rank keeps its drag handle and arrow buttons at 44px and the label wraps, and padding shrinks. Text stays 16px. There is no horizontal scroll at 320px.

Option rows inside a questionnaire (radio, checkbox, and poll result rows) are 56px minimum at every width. This is an accepted exception to the compact density spec. It applies inside PATH-H only. Dense agent tools keep their own row height.
